The sliding contact is moved to end P of the potentiometer and then to end Q.
What are the two readings of the voltmeter?
sliding contact

A

hints: Notice the bottom wire is a common point: the bottom of the potentiometer at P and the bottom of the right-hand $3\text{ V}$ cell are joined.
Connect slider position to potentiometer p.d.: at P the p.d. between slider and P is $0\text{ V}$, while at Q it is the full $3\text{ V}$ across the potentiometer.
Think of the voltmeter as reading slider potential minus the potential at its $-$ terminal, so the right-hand $3\text{ V}$ cell and the slider-to-P p.d. add with the given $+$ to slider polarity.
walkthrough: Take P as $0\text{ V}$ reference. The left $3\text{ V}$ supply is connected across the potentiometer, so $V_P = 0\text{ V}$ and $V_Q = 3\text{ V}$ above P.

The voltmeter $+$ lead is on the slider and the $-$ lead connects through the right-hand $3\text{ V}$ cell back to P, so the meter reads $(V_{slider} - V_P)$ plus the $3\text{ V}$ cell with aiding polarity.
At end P, $V_{slider} = V_P$, so the potentiometer contributes $0\text{ V}$. The loop still contains the right-hand cell, so the reading is $3\text{ V}$.
At end Q, $V_{slider} - V_P = 3\text{ V}$. This acts in the same sense as the right-hand cell for the $+$ to slider connection.
Add the two contributions: $3\text{ V} + 3\text{ V} = 6\text{ V}$, with positive sign matching the $+$ and $-$ markings. This is option D.

A.explanation: This ignores the separate $3\text{ V}$ cell in series with the voltmeter, which still gives a p.d. even when the potentiometer p.d. is zero.

B.explanation: The reading at P is not $0\text{ V}$ because the voltmeter loop still contains the $3\text{ V}$ cell when the slider is at P.

C.explanation: The reading does not stay at $3\text{ V}$ because moving the slider from P to Q adds the full $3\text{ V}$ of the potentiometer to the voltmeter loop.

D.explanation: At P the voltmeter reads only the $3\text{ V}$ cell, and at Q the $3\text{ V}$ potentiometer p.d. adds to give $6\text{ V}$ with the shown polarity.
